<div class="banner">
<strong>Internal working draft</strong> — a team summary of the LTH phenotype results, now updated with the preliminary RNA-seq genetic-label caveat. Not for circulation outside the group.
</div>

A quick tour of what the phenotype half of LTH shows. We heated *A. pulchra* fragments (<span class="t28">28 °C</span> vs <span class="t31">31 °C</span>), wounded half of them, and tracked healing, growth, physiology, and symbionts for two weeks. The phenotype story is already clear: chronic heat depresses colony condition, blocks the final new-corallite step of regeneration while sparing wound closure, and affects fragments from source thicket C far less than fragments from source thickets A and D. Rachael's preliminary RNA-seq SNP/kinship check changes the genetic wording: C looks coherent, but A and D appear mixed, so this summary now treats A/C/D as source-thicket labels rather than verified genets.

Every number here traces to `output/tables/20_master_results.csv`; the full write-up with limitations is in `RESULTS.docx`. Coral photos and the design schematic are from the project deck (M. Brzezinski) — see `img/SLIDE_IMAGES_INDEX.docx`.

## The experiment

- 8 tanks — four held at <span class="t28">28 °C</span> (ambient), four at <span class="t31">31 °C</span> (chronic heat, weeks)
- Half the fragments wounded (clipped growing tip), half sham
- 3 field source thickets — A, C, D (source labels, not yet verified genets)
- Tracked at Days 1, 3, 10, 15

```{r, fig.cap=cap_design}
knitr::include_graphics(img("slide05_experimental_design.png"))
```

We wound a fragment by clipping the growing tip; here is a wounded polyp at Day 0.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_wound_day0}
knitr::include_graphics(img("slide14_morphology_heated_D0.png"))
```

## What we found

### 1. The +3 °C heat treatment held

Tanks sat cleanly at <span class="t28">28</span> vs <span class="t31">31 °C</span> for the whole run — the +3 °C contrast is real, not noise.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_apex}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("08_apex_temperature.png"))
```

### 2. Heat, not wounding, drove colony-wide decline

Under <span class="t31">31 °C</span>, corals lost photosynthetic efficiency, paled, gained less skeletal mass, and shed symbionts.

That distinction matters: wound main effects and heat × wound terms were weak for Fv/Fm, color, growth, and symbiont density. The colony-wide physiology response is therefore primarily a temperature response, not wounded fragments simply falling apart.

- Fv/Fm and color declined through time under heat.
- Symbiont density collapsed over the two weeks.
- Skeletal mass gain was **34% lower** at <span class="t31">31 °C</span>; the tank-level test was marginal (*p* = 0.057), so growth is directionally consistent but weaker than the Fv/Fm, color, and symbiont results.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_growth}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("05_buoyant_weight_growth.png"))
```

```{r, fig.cap=cap_symbiont}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("06_symbiont_density_by_day.png"))
```

### 3. Heat spared wound closure but blocked new corallites

Wounds close at the same rate whether or not corals are heated — and heated corals also **reform the axial polyp and a tip**. What they largely fail to do is bud the **new corallites** (new calyx cups) that mark true skeletal regeneration.

To be exact about what "not regenerated" means, here is the Day-15 breakdown for wounded corals (fraction of corals positive; n = 12 per treatment):

| Trait (Day 15, wounded) | 28 °C | 31 °C |
|---|---|---|
| Wound sealed (`wound_smoothed`) | 100% | 100% |
| Axial polyp formed (`axial_polyp_formation`) | 100% | 100% |
| Tip present (`tip_exist`) | 92% | 92% |
| Tip extended (`tip_extension`) | 92% | 75% |
| **New corallites budded (`new_corallites_on_tip`)** | **100%** | **33%** |

The same split appears in the microscope-photo subset (n = 8 fragments per temperature): new corallites reached 100% of ambient fragments but only 25% of heated fragments by Day 15, matching the main morphology cohort (100% vs 33%).

The healing traits — and even a reformed tip and polyp — are essentially identical between temperatures. The entire signal is one trait, `new_corallites_on_tip`: the budding of *new* skeletal corallites on the tip. That is what "not regenerated" means here, and it is what the survival models test:

- New-corallite budding stalls under heat (interval-censored time ratio **1.32**, *p* = 1.4e-7; Cox HR **0.22**)
- **67%** of heated corals closed the wound and reformed a tip but never budded new corallites, vs **0%** at ambient

```{r, fig.cap=cap_morph_km}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("14_morphology_KM.png"))
```

In the photo timeline below, both temperatures seal the wound and reform a tip; the difference is whether *new corallites* bud on it (the small new calyx cups). Look for those, not the tip itself.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_timeline}
knitr::include_graphics(img("slide15_morphology_timeline.jpg"))
```

Same thing as time-lapse — ambient (left) heals and buds new corallites; heated (right) heals and reforms a tip but stalls before new-corallite budding (loops, D0 → D15):

```{r, results='asis'}

  '<figure style="display:inline-block;width:49%%;margin:0.3em 0;text-align:center;vertical-align:top">
   <video autoplay loop muted playsinline class="content-img" style="width:100%%">
   <source src="data:video/mp4;base64,%s" type="video/mp4"></video>
   <figcaption>%s</figcaption></figure>',
  xfun::base64_encode(img(f)), cap)

        "Ambient time-lapse: wound closure progresses to tip reformation and new-corallite budding by Day 15."),
    vid("morphology_heated_healing.mp4",

```

### 4. Source thicket C was less heat sensitive

The three source thickets did not respond alike. Fragments from source **C** held their photochemistry, color, and symbionts far better than fragments from sources A and D.

The result is strongest as **source-dependent heat sensitivity**, not as baseline physiological differences among groups. Fv/Fm, color, and symbiont density all show source-specific heat trajectories; growth points the same direction but is weaker.

- Heat hit C about **2.7–3.5× less** than A/D (per response — e.g. symbiont loss ~3.5× steeper, Fv/Fm ~2.6× steeper in A/D)
- Multivariate displacement under heat: C = 1.02 vs A = 3.71, D = 3.38

The first plot is the clean read: average heat penalties by source and response domain.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_source_summary}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("19e_source_heat_penalty_summary.png"))
```

Read it left to right: C is near zero overall; A and D carry the bigger physiology/growth and regeneration penalties; wound-closure traits sit near or below zero because closure itself was not slowed by heat.

For the whole-colony physiology responses alone, C has the smaller heat penalty in every response.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_source_physiology}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("19f_source_physiology_heat_penalties.png"))
```

The full response-level audit is below for checking exactly which physiology and morphology traits feed the composite.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_genet_dashboard}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("19_genet_dashboard.png"))
```

The wounded-only morphology summary breaks out the timing milestones separately.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_wound_heat}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("19d_wound_healing_heat_penalties.png"))
```

**How "heat sensitivity" is computed** (`code/19`) — a per-source-thicket composite of finite standardized heat effects:

- **Four physiology/growth responses**: a model-estimated 31 °C vs 28 °C contrast at the response's relevant endpoint — PAM and color at Day 14, symbiont density at the final biopsy, and growth as a start-to-end response. These contrasts are averaged over wound state, so both wounded and unwounded corals contribute.
- **Six wounded-only morphology milestones**: a per-source-thicket **Cox hazard ratio** for time-to-first-onset, so timing enters as the hazard rather than as a single endpoint value.
- Each effect is **row-max scaled** within its own response (largest absolute heat effect in that row = 1), then averaged per source thicket.

So the comparison is not mixing raw values collected on different days. It compares response-specific heat effects after putting them on a common relative scale, includes the unwounded treatments for the physiology metrics, and handles time two ways (endpoint contrasts for physiology/growth, hazards for morphology). It is a **relative ranking** of the three source thickets — a synthesis for the figure, not a formal test. Finite effects averaged: A = 9, C = 10, D = 10. Composite: C = 0.01 vs A = 0.56, D = 0.43.

### 5. What the RNA-seq changes

Preliminary RNA-seq PCA and SNP/kinship results from Rachael's 1 Sept 2026 note suggest that the field labels are not all clean genetic individuals. Source C clusters separately, but sources A and D are intermixed and appear to include several putative genotypes, with some clusters shared between A and D.

That changes the claim, not the phenotype pattern. We should say **source thicket C was less heat sensitive**, not **genet C was less heat sensitive**, until the full SNP run is finalized. The RNA-seq handoff is to join sample-level SNP clusters, genetic PCs, or a kinship matrix back to the phenotype table and ask whether the source-C heat-resilience pattern remains after genetic relatedness is modeled directly.

### 6. The heat treatment was chronic, but sublethal

<span class="t31">31 °C</span> sits about **4.4 °C below** the acute Fv/Fm ED50 (35.4 °C; Cunning et al. 2024) for this species at this site. So this is weeks of sub-bleaching stress, not an acute heat shock — the decline is accumulated, not a spike.

```{r, fig.cap=cap_thermal_context}
knitr::include_graphics(fig("26_thermal_context.png"))
```

## Take-homes

- Chronic sub-bleaching heat drove colony-wide decline: Fv/Fm, color, and symbionts fell strongly, and skeletal growth was lower but marginal at the tank level.
- Wounding did not materially amplify those whole-colony declines.
- Wounds still **healed** under heat, and heated corals reformed a tip and polyp, but they often failed to bud **new corallites** (`new_corallites_on_tip`: 33% vs 100%; 67% sealed the wound and reformed a tip yet never budded new corallites, vs 0% at ambient).
- The regeneration failure repeated in the microscope-photo subset: new-corallite budding was 100% at ambient but only 25% under heat by Day 15.
- Source identity mattered mainly through heat sensitivity, not baseline physiology: fragments from source C were markedly more resilient, so which field material you pick changes the outcome.
- Preliminary RNA-seq SNP/kinship results mean A/C/D should be treated as source-thicket labels for now, not verified genotypes; the next step is to test whether the source-C pattern holds after accounting for SNP clusters, genetic PCs, or kinship.
- At <span class="t31">31 °C</span>, this was chronic sub-bleaching stress (~4.4 °C under the acute ED50), not acute shock.
